entries.reason: extract-zip has no patched release upstream (latest is 2.0.1, advisory covers <=2.0.1). It is pulled in only by @lhci/cli -> lighthouse -> puppeteer-core -> @puppeteer/browsers, a dev-only Lighthouse CI tool that downloads Chrome from Google's own endpoints; it is not part of the production image. Re-check on expiry: upgrade @lhci/cli if a release drops the chain.
entries.fixPlan: On or before expiry: check for an extract-zip release newer than 2.0.1 or an @lhci/cli release newer than 0.15.1 that drops the puppeteer/extract-zip chain, upgrade, and delete these entries. If neither exists, consider replacing @lhci/cli with a direct lighthouse + playwright invocation before renewing.

entries.reason: GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5: memory exhaustion when an array schema without a length cap receives a huge array; denial of service, no data exposure. Fixed only in zod 4.6.6 (a major upgrade). Unbounded arrays exist in src/lib/validation/api-schemas.ts (report sections and findings); it was not confirmed that every route parsing them authenticates first, so treat it as reachable without sign-in. Accepted for a short window so the Next.js RCE fix (v4.7.2) is not held behind the zod 4 migration (Jason, 2026-10-29).
entries.fixPlan: v4.7.3 (maintenance, Codex pre-deploy pass): zod ^4.6.7, which also clears openai and chromium-bidi; then delete these three entries. zod defines the agent tools' argument schemas that LangChain turns into the JSON Schema the model sees, so the move is output-affecting and is proven on staging with real questions, not folded into a security patch.
